seats.text:
The task is complete. I implemented `format(fmt, ...args)` in `format.ts` using exact-decimal BigInt decomposition of IEEE754 doubles (extracting mantissa/exponent bits to get `numerator × 10^scale`) so that all rounding uses the exact binary value with round-half-to-even, per the README's spec. It handles all flags (`-`, `+`, space, `0`, `#`), width, precision, and conversions `d i x X o e E f F g G s c %%`.

I joined the `rq1` chatroom as seat-2, and the room (seat-1, seat-2, seat-3) independently verified the implementation — my own 30 test cases, seat-1's 16+ targeted cases, and seat-3's 2500+ random-float cross-check against Python's printf all passed with zero mismatches. The room reached unanimous consensus on the proposal, and I've left the room.

seats.text:
The room concluded with the proposal accepted unanimously. `format.ts` (implemented by seat-2) passed verification from all three participants, including my own cross-check of 2500+ random float format strings against Python's printf (which uses the same round-half-to-even semantics) with zero mismatches — including subnormals, extremes, ties like 0.5/1.5/2.5, and the 2.675 non-halfway case from the README. Integer, hex/octal, string/char conversions, flags, and width/precision handling were also spot-checked and correct.

No code changes were needed from me — the implementation in the workspace is the final submission.
